items.raw_snippet: Every year, the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI (HAI) publishes the AI Index – the most comprehensive, independently verified overview of the state of AI. Most summaries of it read like a scientific digest. This one is written for those who will need to make practical decisions: what the 2026 data actually means for your implementation decisions, your hiring, your budget, and where AI is and isn’t ready to do real work. Every figure comes from that single, carefully crafted report, so [...] The most useful insight for anyone making these decisions is the distinction between automation and augmentation. Where AI completely automates a task (such as writing standard code or handling routine support chats), demand for entry-level positions tends to decline. Where AI helps people, for example by solving problems or checking their work, employment levels remain stable or even increase. The main question is not whether to “implement AI or not”, it’s how you use it. Teams that use AI to [...] In 2025, artificial intelligence moved from laboratory demonstrations to becoming practical scientific tools. Astronomy has launched its first foundation model, AION-1 (with up to 3 billion parameters), which was trained on 120 terabytes of data covering more than 200 million celestial objects. items.snippet:
Sean knows something about figuring things out along the way.

Before his curren...
items.raw_snippet:
Sean knows something about figuring things out along the way.

Before his current role, he founded a company and experienced both the highs and the difficult realities of building a business. After running out of money and laying off almost the entire team, the company rebuilt by becoming more disciplined, listening directly to customers, and finding new ways to grow.

Seven years later, the company was cash-flow positive and generating real revenue. [...] Following Confluent’s acquisition by IBM in early 2026, Confluent’s AI group is still relatively small while building something new inside a much larger company. That can give people significant responsibility early, whether they are shipping a product from scratch, closing a customer or helping shape how the organization talks about space externally.

“Nobody is walking around with all the answers. If you’d rather figure things out than be handed a spec, this is a good place for that.” [...] “Once you can deliver the right trustworthy data to the model at the right moment, the AI part gets a lot easier,” said Sean.

## Building for what comes next

Sean and his team are thinking beyond AI that simply retrieves and summarizes information.

His vision is AI that can increasingly take work off the business’s plate: approving a transaction, rerouting a shipment, or catching a problem before it becomes one.
